sentence_of_record: On the frozen 300-match canary, epoch 2 reads NO ALARM (d32 21/300 = 0.070 against the 0.138 bar, under both conventions). The same-session rung disagrees on 28/300 = 0.093 [0.060, 0.127], and Δ = −0.023 [−0.057, +0.010] contains zero at every bootstrap seed. The six pairwise disagreements over four passes (0.067–0.093) show no elapsed-time gradient, and the pass labels are exchangeable within match (p = 0.20). At this resolution, the canary measures retest noise and no drift. plain_description.what: Re-judges a frozen set of 300 matches about two days later and again in the same session (1,200 calls). It counts how often the judge's verdict changes.
plain_description.why: It checks whether the judge drifts over time beyond its normal retest noise, which would undermine every comparison made with it.
plain_description.information: A disagreement rate above 0.138 would raise the drift alarm and flag later judged numbers for re-reading. Result: no alarm. Verdicts changed on 7% of matches after about two days and on 9.3% within the same session, with no time trend. At this resolution the canary measures retest noise and finds no drift. Drift smaller than about 4.5 points cannot be ruled out. The frozen match set comes from the older question pool, which was later ruled history rather than evidence.
